tool_input.command:
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(daemon): sign splices signatures instead of a destructive re-marshal (FIX 2, FIX 4)

Four findings, one repair to `beadle-daemon sign`:

1. The round-trip guard was tautological. canon and the argument to
   VerifySignature were both CanonicalCommandBytes(&command) on the SAME
   struct value -- byte-equal by construction, proving nothing about
   whether the file actually written to disk would load.
2. It destroyed the recipe. yaml.Marshal(&command) dumped every field with
   no omitempty: comments vanished, zero-value fields materialized.
3. Content could be silently altered: yaml.v3 loses a leading newline in a
   string scalar on a marshal/unmarshal round trip.
4. The write truncated in place instead of write-temp-then-rename.

Fix: splice the new signature into the ORIGINAL file bytes (stripping any
existing `signature:` key first), write to path+".signing" (never .yaml --
LoadCommands globs *.yaml), decode THAT file independently and compare its
canonical bytes to what was actually signed (the real, non-tautological
check), then separately run daemon.VerifySignature (a distinct check: it
fails on a stale/wrong signer key and reports itself as a signature
failure, not a bytes mismatch), then os.Rename into place. Any failure
refuses to write -- it never normalizes the recipe to make it pass.

Also in this change, since splitting it would produce four conflicting
edits to the same functions:

- Canonical form moves from YAML to JSON (Command gains json tags,
  omitempty on every slice field so a nil slice and a round-tripped empty
  slice canonicalize identically -- json.Marshal, unlike yaml.v3,
  distinguishes null from [], and this asymmetry alone broke the daemon's
  own test harness fixtures once JSON was adopted). This invalidates
  existing signatures, intended and free -- nothing is released yet.
- One shared daemon.DecodeCommandFile, used by loadCommand, `sign`,
  `verify`, and sign's own readback of the re-signed file. Three
  hand-maintained copies existed before.
- sign validates a COPY of the decoded command (daemon.ValidateCommand,
  newly exported) before signing, so an invalid recipe never signs green
  and fails only later, at daemon startup. The copy matters:
  ValidateCommand writes scalar defaults, and loadCommand verifies a
  signature BEFORE it validates, so the signed bytes must stay pre-default.
- sign compares --signer against daemon.json's authorizer key (reusing
  verify's existing resolveVerifySigner) and refuses a mismatch unless
  --force.

FIX 4, same mission, folded in here because it also touches `init`'s
signature: `init` now probes the authorizer key with pgp.CheckKeyExpiry
before writing daemon.json -- absent-from-keyring and non-expiring-key
both surface at init time instead of days later, at the far end of the
pipeline, as a wrong-key/key-expired rejection with no link back to the
typo. --no-verify-key is the explicit escape for configuring a key before
it has been imported on this machine. Five existing init tests asserted
success with a synthetic fingerprint in no keyring; they now use a real
generated key (two of them prove the probe's positive and negative cases
directly) or pass --no-verify-key where key validity isn't what the test
is about. init's own daemon.json write also moved to write-temp-then-
rename, matching persist.go's existing pattern in this package.

Also: verify_cmd.go's SignatureError branch now wraps with %w instead of
formatting it away, so errors.As can recover the verdict from the error
runVerify returns (FIX 7); sign's passphrase credential name is now
secret.CredGPGPassphrase instead of a second hand-maintained copy of the
same string (FIX 7, internal/secret/secret.go).

TestRunSign_RoundTrip is table-driven over every file in
examples/recipes/*.yaml rather than one minimal five-scalar fixture, so
coverage grows when a recipe is added and the fixpoint property is proven
somewhere it could actually break (docs-ask.yaml omits `mode`, exercising
the pre-default canonicalization ordering the tautological guard could
never have caught either).

Verified end to end against a real GPG key, outside the test suite: init
(including the negative unimported-key and --no-verify-key cases), sign
(comment preservation, --force mismatch override), verify (good and
tampered), and a genuinely signed sysreport.yaml loading through the real
daemon.LoadCommands entry point.
EOF
)"
